messages.content: my friend and i wanted a walk, but there is rain now. she asked if we should leave the whole visit for another day.
do you still want to see her inside, or was the walk the part you most wanted?
i want to see her. the walk was just a way to spend the time.
then you can ask whether she would like to visit at home instead. the place can change while the time together can stay part of the plan.
write a simple message to her.
i would still like to see you. would you like to come here instead of going for a walk?
she says she does not want to make me cook a meal. i had not thought about food yet.
you can tell her it can be a simple visit. having someone over does not have to mean making a whole meal.
what could i say with tea?
we can just have tea and talk. i do not need to make a meal.
can that sound like i will not let her eat if she is hungry?
you can keep it about your plan rather than a rule for her. i was thinking of tea and a talk, not a whole meal.
now she says that sounds good. what have we chosen?
you have chosen to visit inside with tea and conversation instead of going for a walk.
use inside in the answer.
you have chosen to visit inside with tea and conversation instead of going for a walk.
only give a warm last reply now.
it sounds like the time together was the important part.
write a story about a father and his child looking at a picture he made when he was young. the child should learn something about trying, not that everyone must draw the same way.

a father was looking through an old book when a drawing came out from between the pages. his child asked who had made it. he said it was his, from when he was young. the picture had a large house, a small door, and a tree that almost went to the top of the page. the child had a laugh at the size of the tree, then looked at a new drawing on her own table. she had been worried because her tree was large too. her father said he had not known much about drawing when he made the old picture, but he had enjoyed trying. they put the old and new pictures together for a moment. each could tell a story without every line being right. the child took her own paper back and chose to add a person under the tree.
what did the father say about drawing when he was young?
he had not known much about it, but he had enjoyed trying.
did he tell the child to make her tree smaller?
no. he showed his old picture and talked about trying. she chose what to add to her own.
can you tell the first part in the voice of the child?
my father found a drawing he had made when he was young. i had not known it was his until i asked.
give that with i had not known.
my father found a drawing he had made when he was young. i had not known it was his until i asked.
now just give a sentence about her choice at the end.
she chose to add a person under the tree in her own picture.
what is different between the book is in the container and i put the book into the container?
the first gives where the book is. the other gives a change: you move the book from outside to inside the container.
can i say i put the book in the container too?
yes. put the book in the container can be clear about the same change. into can make the idea of going inside clear.
say it with going inside.
into can make the idea of going inside clear. put in can also work in that sentence.
now make a sentence where the book is already inside and i only move the container.
i moved the container while the book stayed inside it.
does moving the container always mean i took the book out?
no. in that sentence, it stayed inside. moving the container and taking out the book are different things.
now the container is on a shelf. where is the book?
inside the container on the shelf.
what if i ask where it is without saying book or container?
i would ask which object you mean if the context is not clear.
ask that question.
which object do you mean: the book or the container?
the container. full sentence, please.
the container is on the shelf.
how was your day?
i do not have a day in the way a person does, but i am here to talk with you. how has your day been?
i wanted a kind answer, not a long explanation about being a model.
hello. i am here to talk. how are you doing?
keep it kind and simple.
hello. i am here to talk. how are you doing?
i had a quiet morning and a busy afternoon.
what was the quiet part of the morning like?
i read near the window before work. i would like more of that, but i do not want to wake up before i usually do.
you can like that quiet time without choosing a whole new morning plan right now. it can simply be a part of today you enjoyed.
i mean before i usually wake up. please do not give me a new plan.
you enjoyed reading before work today. you do not need to choose a new time to wake up just to say it was good.
can you reply without another plan?
it sounds like a calm start before a busy afternoon.
that is enough. just goodbye.
goodbye. i hope the rest of your day goes well.
help me ask my cousin to have lunch with me tomorrow. i know the day i want, but not the place.
would you like to have lunch together tomorrow? we can choose a place that works for both of us.
can i make it less like every detail is open? i want the restaurant near the park if she likes it.
would you like lunch tomorrow at the restaurant near the park? we can choose another place if that does not work for you.
she says tomorrow is good but she does not like that restaurant. what should i keep and what should i change?
keep tomorrow as the chosen day, and leave the restaurant open. you can ask what place she would like instead.
write the reply.
tomorrow works. what place would you like instead?
she says at my house. does my mean my house as the person writing now, or hers?
in her message, my house is her house. when you tell someone else about it, you would say her house.
now write my answer to her saying yes.
yes. lunch at your house tomorrow works for me.
can you choose an hour in the same answer?
not unless you give an hour. you can ask what time would work.
only give that last question.
what time would work for lunch?
write a story about a person who wants music and another who wants quiet. they should ask each other questions before choosing what to do.

a sister and brother were in the living room after school. she wanted to listen to music, while he was trying to understand a hard page. when she went to turn on the radio, he asked whether she could wait for a little while. she thought he was talking about the whole evening and began to feel sad. he explained that he only wanted time to finish the page. she asked whether a few minutes would be enough. he said he was not sure, but he could tell her when he was done. she took her own book to the kitchen for a while. later, he came to say the page was more clear and asked what music she wanted. they turned on the radio together. neither had got everything at once, but both had said what they needed.
why did she first think the answer was no for the whole evening?
she thought wait for a little while might mean a long wait. asking more made the request more clear.
say it with more clear.
asking more made the request more clear.
did the brother know the specific number of minutes?
no. he said he was not sure and would tell her when he was done.
give the question she asked about time.
would a few minutes be enough?
can you tell me one of them was always right and the other always wrong?
no. they wanted different things and asked about how the time could work for both.
now only give a short name for the story.
a page before the music.
i read a blue book, a red book, and then the blue book again. how many different books did i read?
two different books: the blue one and the red one.
can i say i had three parts of reading, with the same blue book in two of them?
yes. you had three parts of reading, but only two different books.
now i read a green book. how many different books?
three different books.
what if i read only one page of the green book?
then you have read from three different books, but you have not said you finished all three. a page is not a whole book.
can you put those facts in a short sentence in my voice?
i read from three different books, and i read the blue one again.
does that say the red book was read again too?
no. only the blue book was said to be read again.
now i add that i finished the red and blue books, but not the green one. how many did i finish?
you finished the red book and the blue book.
use book in the answer.
you finished the red book and the blue book.
only give the number of different books i read from.
three.
my friend stopped coming to the reading group. i think it must be because she did not like the book, but she has not said why.
you do not yet know her reason. the book could be part of it, or the time, place, or something outside the group could be important.
write a question that does not choose the reason for her.
would you like to talk about why you stopped coming to the group?
she says the time no longer works because of her work.
then the reason she gave is the time and her work, not the book.
can i tell the group she did not like the book?
not from what she said. you would be changing the reason she gave.
what if i want to ask whether another time would help?
would another time work better for you?
she says maybe, but she is not ready to choose.
then you can leave the choice open and tell her she can let you know later if she wants.
write a kind reply without asking another question.
okay. you can let me know later if you want to try another time.
does that say i must change the group time before she chooses?
no. it leaves her choice open. it does not make a whole new group plan.
is all of us wrote a letter the same as each of us wrote a letter?
not always. all of us wrote a letter can sound like the group wrote one letter together. each of us wrote a letter makes one letter for each person more clear.
use one letter for each person.
each of us wrote a letter makes one letter for each person more clear. all of us can be about the group doing it together.
what if there are three people and one letter, with each person putting a name on it?
then you can say: we all wrote one letter together and each put a name on it.
what if each person wrote two messages?
with three people each writing two messages, there would be six messages.
now make the sentence with each before person.
each person wrote two messages.
why not each people?
each person talks about one person at a time. people is the group word, while person is one.
now ask how many messages each person wrote.
how many messages did each person write?
why write after did instead of wrote?
after did in that question, use write. in the answer, each person wrote two messages is right.
only give the sentence about one letter together again.
we all wrote one letter together and each put a name on it.
i found a photo of me holding a book when i was a child. i do not remember that day, but i know the house in the picture.
you can know a place without a memory of every day you were there. what do you remember about the house?
the kitchen table and the sound of the door. it was the home of my aunt.
those details can be part of your memory of the place, even if the photo gives a day you cannot place.
i mean i know the house but not the day. help me write it in my voice.
i found a photo of myself as a child with a book in my hands. i know it was taken at the home of my aunt, but i do not remember the day.
can i add the table and door without saying they were in the photo?
yes. keep them as things you remember about the house, not things you must see in the photo.
write it with i remember.
i found a photo of myself at the home of my aunt. i do not remember the day, but i remember the kitchen table and the sound of the door there.
does that say the sound is inside the picture?
no. the sound is part of your memory of the house, not something the photo itself gives.
now just give a warm reply about the memory of a place.
it sounds like the picture brought back a good part of your memory of that house.
write a story about two people getting a room ready for a visit. one has less time, but both should help without doing the same work.

a father and daughter wanted to get the living room ready before their cousin came. the father had only a few minutes before a work call, while the daughter had more time. they looked at what needed to be done and chose different parts. he carried books from the sofa to the shelf and put a chair near the table. she put paper in order and took the cups to the kitchen. before his call, he asked whether there was one more thing he could do. she asked him to move a small table away from the door. after he went to work, she finished the last part. when their cousin came, the room had space to sit and talk. the father had not done as many things, but he had used the time he had to help.
did both people do the same work?
no. one had less time, so they chose different parts of the work.
did the father do nothing?
no. he helped with books, a chair, and a small table before his call.
why did the daughter finish the last part?
she had more time after he went to work.
can you make the end in the voice of the daughter?
my father had less time, but he helped with the books, chair, and table. i did the other parts, and the room was ready when our cousin came.
does doing less always mean less care?
no. the number of things done does not by itself give how much care someone has.
only give the question he asked before his call.
is there one more thing i can do before my call?
i have chosen what to do. i want to try the small plan tomorrow, not keep thinking about ten other plans.
okay. you can leave the other plans for now and try the one you chose.
say it with leave the other plans for now.
you can leave the other plans for now and try the one you chose.
can you reply without telling me it will work for sure?
i hope the small plan helps, and you can learn from trying it.
what if i just want a goodbye without another idea about learning?
goodbye. i hope your day goes well.
now one word.
goodbye.
